items.title: Step 1 of the fit method — measure the band
items.body: Measure snugly under the bust, with the tape level and the exhale relaxed. In most sizing systems this under-bust number is the band size. If you are between two band numbers, the comfortable choice is usually the larger band with the same cup letter — a band that rides up is the most common comfort complaint. This is a general convention, not a brand-specific claim.

items.title: Step 2 — measure the full bust, then work out the cup
items.body: Measure around the fullest part of the bust without compressing. The difference between that and the under-bust measurement maps to a cup letter. A common starting convention is roughly one inch for A, two for B and three for C, but cup increments are not standardised across brands and Indian labels sometimes differ. Use the exact brand's chart when you have one.

items.title: Step 3 — sister sizing and the comfort test
items.body: Sister sizes keep the cup volume while changing the band: go down a band and up a cup, or up a band and down a cup, and the cup volume stays broadly similar. For wireless comfort bras, the practical test is simple: raise your arms — the band should stay put, the cups should not gap, and nothing should dig into the armpit. Test at home with tags intact.

items.body: Do not pay on the assumption that NUASOFT30, TRY35 or TRY20 are active. None was verified on 26 Nov 2026 — read the live code box instead.
Confirm which business is actually selling at the URL you opened. A domain can change hands or be repurposed; the product page, not an old article, identifies the seller.
If the store does list bras, take your under-bust and full-bust measurements and match them to that store's own chart, not to the generic method here.
Where returns allow, order two adjacent sizes in one style rather than two different styles — it isolates fit from design.
Keep tags and packaging intact until after the at-home wear test; inspect-on-return policies commonly depend on tags being attached.
For running, high-impact training or post-surgery needs, buy a purpose-built sports or medical-support product instead of a lifestyle comfort bra.

content_blocks.text: We fetched nuawoman.com, a bra-collection path and nua.in on 26 Nov 2026. The domain served period-care content rather than the lingerie catalogue described in the earlier guide, and we could not verify the codes, cup range or factory claims carried over from that copy. Where verification failed, we have said so rather than filling the page with plausible-sounding product detail. Durza earns a commission on qualifying purchases through tracked links at no extra cost to you.

items: A domain name is not a guarantee that the original brand still trades there — always check the seller and product page.
Cup-letter increments are not globally standardised; the same label can fit differently across brands and countries.
Sister sizing preserves approximate cup volume, not an identical fit on every body.
A home fit check is a screening step. Persistent rubbing, peeling or skin irritation needs a clinician, not a different size guess.
The fit method here is our editorial contribution. It is not a Nuawoman, Nua or manufacturer size chart.

items.q: Is Nuawoman still selling wireless bras?
items.a: We could not confirm that on 26 Nov 2026. nuawoman.com served a Nua period-care and intimate-hygiene store, and the /collections/bras path returned no bra products. If you land on a page that does sell bras, check the seller identity before ordering — do not rely on this old guide's product descriptions.

items.q: Do NUASOFT30, TRY35 or TRY20 still work?
items.a: We did not verify any of them. They appeared in older Durza copy, but no live page we fetched on 26 Nov 2026 confirmed them. Only a code accepted in your own cart is evidence that it works for your order.

items.q: How do I pick a comfortable wireless bra size?
items.a: Measure under the bust for the band and over the fullest point for the cup, then follow the specific brand's chart because cup increments are not standardised. If the band fits but the cup does not, try a sister size. At home, raise your arms and check for band slip, cup gap and armpit dig-in.

items.q: Is this a Nuawoman size chart?
items.a: No. It is a general comfort fit method written by Durza, and it is offered precisely because the brand's own chart could not be verified on the live domain. Use the seller's chart whenever one is available.

items.q: Did Durza buy or test any lingerie for this guide?
items.a: No. We checked live web pages on 26 Nov 2026, purchased nothing and make no comfort, support or fabric-performance claims.
